github_release.body:
SmolBox is an Elixir client and supervised execution runtime for self-hosted SmolVM 1.14.1 workers. Run code in disposable VMs while keeping execution identities, observed outcomes, cancellation and cleanup explicit.

```elixir
{:smolbox, "~> 0.1.0"}
```

[Hex package](https://hex.pm/packages/smolbox/0.1.0) · [API documentation](https://hexdocs.pm/smolbox/0.1.0/) · [Getting started](https://hexdocs.pm/smolbox/0.1.0/getting-started.html)

This first release includes:

- Typed client operations for worker health, VM lifecycle, commands, output streams and binary files.
- Explicit supervision, immutable execution identities, duplicate/conflict handling, admission, recovery, cancellation and bounded cleanup. Uncertain commands are never silently replayed.
- Store and artifact-store contracts, a bounded in-memory store, and complete minimal and PostgreSQL host examples.
- User guides, troubleshooting, telemetry and compatibility evidence for Linux x86_64/KVM and macOS Apple Silicon.

The release was validated on eight Elixir/OTP/platform combinations, including Elixir 1.20.4/OTP 29.0.6 on both platforms, with analyzer, coverage, live-runtime, durable-recovery and package-consumer checks. Its runtime code and persisted formats are unchanged from RC2.

This release targets development environments. Production resource/isolation certification is outside its supported scope. Unsupported hard controls remain rejected, and documented upstream execution-fencing and path-containment limitations remain. Read [Deployment boundaries](https://hexdocs.pm/smolbox/0.1.0/security.html) before choosing a deployment.

[Changelog](https://github.com/hfiguera/smolbox/blob/v0.1.0/CHANGELOG.md)

setup_notes: Hex required an authenticator OTP for publication after OAuth sign-in. The noninteractive attempt was stopped at that prompt, and registry absence was checked before retrying interactively. The successful publication receipt is recorded without the OTP.

The first Hex dry run waited for its interactive confirmation and was terminated before any upload. Its zero process exit does not establish a completed dry run. The successful rerun used --dry-run --yes, built package and docs, and was followed by a byte-identical archive rebuild.
Each host used its own PostgreSQL instance with 30 connections and a private local Unix socket; Linux's shared database was preserved.
Package construction used an additional clean source checkout per host to avoid concurrent Mix operations in runtime test checkouts.
validation: local development hosts plus ordinary hosted GitHub CI
